name: Goan-leaning peri-peri sauce (chile, garlic, lemon, vinegar)
status: PRELIMINARY ESTIMATE — NOT COOKED OR TASTED
shelf_life_note: 3 days at ≤ 5 °C (ASSUMPTION: set by a food-safety professional)

lines.prep: soaked 15 min in hot water, drained

method: Soak the chiles, drain, blend with garlic, passata, lemon, vinegar and water until smooth.
Cook in the oil 8-10 min, stirring, until the raw-garlic edge is gone and the sauce coats a spoon; season.
Cool in a shallow pan (two-stage cooling) and chill.
food_safety: Two-stage cooling: 57→21 °C within 2 h, then to ≤ 5 °C within a further 4 h.
evidence: Practice: peri-peri (piri-piri) is a chile-garlic-citrus/vinegar sauce associated with Portuguese-influenced cooking including Goa (web-search snippet level only; primary sources not retrieved). NASHA composition is new.
estimates_label: All quantities, yields, times and costs are preliminary estimates until a person cooks and measures them. Nothing here has been cooked or tasted.
